warnings: Official fleet-size and licensing claims beyond CTA Determination A-2025-149 remain self-reported; film credits and search-and-rescue service availability do not establish defence adoption.

Current named Canadian customers and contracts remain unresolved. Radar, optronics, electronic-warfare and mission-management products are group offerings or representation scope, not proven Canadian manufacture or delivery.

The 2026 event is a bounded technical testbed, not production deployment or procurement. Production customers, certifications, government or classified accreditations, data-residency boundaries, scale and current ownership remain unresolved.
TSB investigation A25A0042 remains active, so no cause or fault should be inferred. Current post-accident fleet and operating capacity are not independently established.
First-party customer-use claims are not independent validation. Keep TRAIL distinct from the CSA-funded Open Ground Motion Service and do not infer defence deployment.

The official site supports a present product-sheet and demo-request surface, but commercial transactions, named customers, deployments and quantitative performance remain unverified; do not publish unsupported legacy product branding.

Current official terms locate Blue Ocean Gear in San Francisco, while the stored dossier calls it Halifax-based. Fisheries and Oceans Canada sources verify Canadian pilots and deployments, but do not establish Canadian ownership or headquarters, leaving the project inclusion and Canadian-footprint basis unresolved.

The stored True North Map profile conflates C-Tow Marine Assistance Ltd. with an autonomous-marine-systems company. The exact c-tow.ca domain documents towing, refloating and marine-assistance services, so the current organization and capability identity cannot safely receive an editorial dossier refresh.

Clear Seas identifies itself as an independent Canadian not-for-profit research organization, while the canonical True North Map record is typed as a company. The research and maritime decision-support evidence is strong, but the entity-kind mismatch must be corrected before activating the shared company dossier template.

A July 2026 issuer announcement says Coastal Defence Systems was acquired by Lake Central Air Services and the combined business now operates as Valkyrie Aerospace Corp. The current canonical organization identity is therefore stale and cannot safely receive a routine Coastal Defence Systems dossier activation.

Darkwater's official site identifies it as a division of Enviromarine Ltd., while the canonical True North Map record is typed as a company. The operating evidence is useful, but the entity-kind and parent-record decision must be resolved before the shared company dossier is activated.

Drone Delivery Canada and Volatus completed their merger in August 2024, the issuer became Volatus Aerospace Inc., and DDC now remains a cargo brand. The standalone canonical organization identity is stale and cannot safely receive a routine dossier refresh.

Elbit's current global presence routes Canada to GeoSpectrum Technologies, while Canadian procurement and lobbying records name Elbit Systems Ltd. The standalone Elbit Systems Canada legal entity and Canadian workshare represented by the canonical record remain unresolved.

Scandium Canada announced that it acquired Ferreol's operating company on June 29, 2026 and rebranded it as Scalium+, a wholly owned subsidiary. The legacy Ferreol identity is stale and requires a successor-record decision before dossier activation.

Foresight's 2025 Form 20-F identifies an Israeli company operating from Ness Ziona with Israeli and Chinese subsidiaries, and the audit found no durable Canadian subsidiary, office or operating footprint. The canonical Canada-suffixed identity and inclusion basis are unsupported.

Honeywell Aerospace separated into independent Honeywell Aerospace Inc. on June 29, 2026, while Canadian records still name Honeywell Limited, Honeywell ASCa Inc. and COM DEV-related operations. Public evidence does not establish which Canadian entities and facilities transferred to the new issuer.

IMP's official site describes IMP Aerospace & Defence as an operating business unit of IMP Group Ltd., while the canonical True North Map record is typed as a standalone company. Current Cormorant evidence is useful but cannot repair that entity-kind and parent boundary inside this dossier-only refresh.

The official current brand is IMT Precision, formerly IMT Defence, and an Ontario regulatory record names IMT Partnership as the legal operator. The canonical name and legal identity are stale and require a core rename and lineage decision before dossier activation.

Industrial Recon's official site identifies it as a division of Aliter Technologies 3CIS Inc., while the canonical record is typed as a standalone company. Its offer is an inspection service using third-party platforms, not an OEM portfolio, and no durable current customer signal was recovered.

LeddarTech's official news record ends in May 2025 amid Nasdaq deficiency and financing notices, and the February 2025 unnamed-OEM design win was conditional on definitive agreements. Current 2026 corporate, listing, financing and operating status are unresolved, while defence fit remains automotive-derived.

The canonical True North Map record is a false identity and capability match. Current durable evidence identifies Mecanica as a United States forensic and accident-reconstruction business associated with Oxnard, California, while no Canadian maritime or naval engineering footprint was found.

The canonical True North Map record is a false identity and capability match. Picomole Inc. was a Moncton breath-analysis medical-device company renamed Breathe BioMedical Inc.; the old domain redirects to Breathe BioMedical, not an Ottawa cybersecurity or attack-surface company.

The current product owner is the United States company Quanergy Solutions Inc., created after a 2023 Chapter 11 asset sale, and no durable current Canadian legal entity, office, staff or operating footprint was recovered. The canonical Ottawa and Canadian-company identity is unsupported.

Woodward acquired all equity of the Peterborough Safran Electronics & Defense Canada entity in July 2025 and supplier quality records identify its later name as Woodward Canada Inc. The canonical record also mixes that divested controls business with other Safran Canadian navigation and optronics activities.

Durable sources identify Sierra Space Corporation in Broomfield, Colorado, and no Canadian subsidiary, facility, employees or Canadian customer program was found. The stored Brampton address appears to belong to MDA Space rather than Sierra Space.

The historical Canadian aerial pipeline-monitoring company has no qualified operating signal after 2022, current search results collide with an unrelated United States public company, and Investment Canada evidence indicates foreign control at formation. Current Canadian operation, ownership and customers remain unresolved.

The University of Toronto Space Flight Laboratory became the private SFL Missions Inc. in May 2026, and a July CanadaBuys award now names SFL Missions Inc. The old university-lab canonical identity is stale and the exact corporate, intellectual-property and duplicate-record relationship requires a core lifecycle decision.

Deloitte records that SpaceRyde Inc. made an Assignment in Bankruptcy on February 10, 2023, the official domain no longer resolves, and the federal registry's administratively active status conflicts with overdue filings and an intent-to-dissolve notice. A current supplier dossier would be misleading.

Independent labour and industry evidence records the shutdown of Tangent Animation production and its Toronto and Winnipeg workforce in 2021, while the stored simulation and digital-twin profile and current website continuity could not be reconciled to a surviving operating entity.

A10 Networks acquired TrojAI Inc. in June 2026, so the stored standalone Canadian-company identity and ownership context are stale; the current status of the Fredericton operation, personnel and product continuity requires a core lifecycle decision.

The current site makes consequential claims about Canadian RMUS and Unmanned Systems Poland authorization, Kitchener assembly, platform and operator scale, NATO STANAG 4586 alignment, NDAA options and defence customers, but no independent partner, registry, procurement or program source recovered in the three-lane audit resolved the entity or those authorizations.

De Havilland Aircraft of Canada states that Viking Air Limited and related Longview aviation entities amalgamated into De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited in August 2024, so Viking is no longer a safe standalone current organization record.
